summary: Tested multiple IGSS orders per patient end to end (backend pytest with 14 tests plus Playwright UI). Working: POST /api/patients (the 405 is fixed); creating a patient with 2 different NOGs takes 2 discounts, and the same NOG twice takes only 1; removing one order with PUT frees 1 discount and adding it back takes it again; GET returns igss_ordenes; the lazy migration of legacy NOG/SPS/código shows up in the edit form; manual 'aplicar' gives +1, a duplicate returns 400 and an unknown patient returns 404; 'anular' frees the discount; an evaluation stores its order, autosave changing the order is saved, and the PDF returns 200; agenda appointments store the order, and two appointments for the same patient on the same day with different orders were created. UI: the Órdenes IGSS section shows only for IGSS patients, 'Agregar orden' is disabled until a unit is chosen, rows can be added and removed, and orders are kept after create and edit; the evaluation order card auto-selects the first order and autosaves when it changes; the agenda order selector creates 2 separate appointments; the NOG 'aplicar' box searches (needs at least 2 characters), applies, refreshes the list, shows an error toast on duplicates, and 'Anular' works. Two backend logic bugs found.

critical.issue: Removing ALL orders (igss_ordenes: []) does not work. update_patient sees an empty list and falls back to the patient's stored legacy igss_nog/igss_no_sps/igss_codigo (still those of the old first order), so it rebuilds 1 order and keeps the discount. In the UI, a user who deletes every order row and saves gets the first order back. Fix: only use the legacy fallback when 'igss_ordenes' is NOT in update_data (or also clear the legacy fields when the list is explicitly empty).

A manual discount is silently cancelled the next time the patient is edited (even an unrelated field such as comments). Reconciliation cancels every active acreditación whose nog_id is not among the patient's orders, and a manual one (origen='manual') is never among them. Either exclude origen='manual' from the cancellation in reconciliation, or have 'aplicar' also add an order with that NOG to the patient.

minor.issue: Does not check that the patient is IGSS or belongs to the NOG's unit. A particular patient, or one from another unit, can be discounted (the UI search lists all patients).
Rows show the patient's legacy igss_no_sps/igss_codigo (first order) instead of the SPS/código of the order that matches this NOG. Wrong for the second and later orders.

Pre-existing drift in Zona 11: NOG 12345678 has acreditados=3 but only 1 active acreditación document, and QA-UI-38804 has 3 vs 2. This was already there before my tests, which left net zero; it is probably from earlier test cleanups that hard-deleted documents. 'recalcular' only creates missing acreditaciones and never lowers the counter.

ui_bugs.issue: Every order row uses the same data-testid patient-igss-nog-select / patient-igss-nog, so they are not unique per row. Suggest patient-orden-nog-{idx}.

integration_issues.flow: Edit patient -> delete all orders -> save
integration_issues.issue: The first order comes back after saving (backend fallback bug above).

issues: Applying uses up a service with a single click and no confirmation.
After the duplicate-error toast the result list stays open.
The search has no debounce, so out-of-order responses can show stale results.

action_items: Fix update_patient so an explicit igss_ordenes=[] clears the orders (no legacy fallback) and frees the discounts
Keep manual (origen='manual') acreditaciones during _reconciliar_nog_paciente, or add the NOG as an order to the patient in 'aplicar'
Validate in 'aplicar' that the patient is IGSS and belongs to nog.unidad_id
Show the SPS/código of the order matching the NOG in the NOG patient list and Excel export
Optional: unique testids for the NOG select in each order row; confirmation before a manual discount

_reconciliar_nog_paciente treats every acreditación outside the target NOGs as stale, including manual and evaluation ones

Legacy lazy order id '<patientId>_ord1' exists only in responses; evaluations or appointments that reference it before the patient is saved keep an id that stays consistent once saved (normalize keeps ids), so this is fine
Pacientes.js (1631 lines), EvaluacionOftalmologica.js (3686 lines) and Agenda.js (2736 lines) are well over 700 lines and should be split

rca of the issue: Bug 1: in routes/patients.py update_patient (~line 729-742), when igss_ordenes=[] the list normalizes to empty and the code then falls back to leg_nog = patient.get('igss_nog') (the stored value from the old first order), recreating the order. Bug 2: in routes/igss_nogs.py _reconciliar_nog_paciente, target_ids comes only from the orders, and the loop over 'vigentes' cancels everything outside target_ids, which includes manual acreditaciones. Reproduce both with tests/test_igss_ordenes_multiples.py.
